items.title: Karnataka may face severe water, power shortages amid drought: CM DK Shivakumar
items.summary: Karnataka could face severe shortages of drinking water and electricity in the coming days as drought conditions worsen across the state, Chief Minister DK Shivakumar said on Monday, September 14. Speaking to reporters in Kanakapura, Shivakumar said groundwater levels had fallen sharply and extensive crop damage had been reported amid deficient rainfall. “This year, the groundwater level has fallen drastically, and crops have been destroyed. In many places, crops could not even be cultivated. Going forward, the situation indicates that there could be a severe shortage of drinking water and electricity,” CM DK Shivakumar said during a visit to his home constituency of Kanakapura. Karnataka has already declared 101 taluks drought-hit, while more areas are expected to be added based on prescribed norms and Union government guidelines. Shivakumar said more than 200 of the state’s 239 taluks were facing drought conditions. The rainfall deficit has worsened with the weak monsoon in September.
